body:
# Independent audit: minimum simplex containers and convexification cost


`candidate fb9f38f6d568ee74`
and checked its constants, compactness argument, and all actual-fiber claims.
No companion verifier was present when this audit was performed.

1. The source hull has exactly the fibers stated at integer bases 0, 1, 2.
Grouping coefficients at the endpoint bases gives the middle Minkowski mean.
The planar fiber areas and the pentagon vertices are correct.
2. For an arbitrary point of an enclosing triangle, a barycentric coordinate
at least 1/3 gives a vertex cap of relative area at most 4/9. Thus the middle
absolute-depth upper bound is valid for every point and uses ambient planar
halfspaces. After scaling, its deficit bound is 5ε²/36. The square contributes
ε²/18, so the total is positive and at most 7ε²/36.
3. The family of triangles containing the unit square with area at most 2 is
compact. The disk-diameter cone estimate bounds every vertex within distance
4 of the square center. Every limiting triangle still contains the square,
so degeneracy cannot occur. Support functions are continuous on this family.
4. Each term of the support excess is nonnegative. Equality forces inclusion
in the triangle x,y≥0, 2x+y≤3. The two positive-length square edge contacts
force two distinct triangle facets to lie on the coordinate axes. The corner
(1,1) then forces the sole possible container to have intercepts 3/2 and 3,
and area 9/4. This contradicts the area bound 2. The positive attained support
gap α is therefore justified without classifying square minimum triangles.
5. The polygon Minkowski area identity has the stated coefficients:
|T+εS|=1+ε[2h_S(−e1)+h_S(−e2)+h_S(2e1+e2)]+ε²|S|.
Its first coefficient agrees with the three edge lengths and outward unit
normals of T. The statement includes translated triangles because that
weighted support sum is translation invariant.
6. A minimum enclosing triangle for any compact convex planar body with
interior exists: use one enclosing triangle as an area upper bound; an
inscribed disk and the same diameter-cone argument bound every candidate
vertex; pass to a convergent vertex triple. This proves attainment also for
the middle fiber, although the lower bound is independent of that choice.
The minimum enclosing triangle of T is uniquely T, since a proper convex
superset of a full-dimensional compact convex set has strictly larger area.
7. Convexification at base 1 contains (T+εS)/2 regardless of the chosen middle
container. Formula (13) follows; every other actual-fiber excess is
nonnegative and the projection remains [0,2]. Dividing by 7ε²/36 yields
9α/(7ε), exactly as stated.
8. Binary padding repeats the argument without mixing layers at binary
vertices. It multiplies both quantities by 2^(n−1).

This certifies a counterexample to the minimum-container quantitative bridge,
not to (OC). A stronger obstruction allowing arbitrary enclosing triangles
is developed separately.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
